results.question: When do I send my first unemployment status report to Kela?
results.answer: You must submit your first unemployment status report after you have submitted your first application to Kela [S1]. For the first benefit payment, the report must cover a period of 2 weeks [S1]. Alternatively, if Kela has granted you the benefit, you must submit a report for the first 10 working days you have been unemployed [S3]. You can only report days of unemployment that have already passed [S1][S3]. Visit OmaKela to see when you need to submit your report [S3].

results.question: I'm 22 and have no vocational qualification. Do I have to apply for studies to get the benefit?
results.answer: Yes, if you are under 25 and do not have a vocational qualification or higher education degree, you must apply for admission to at least two study programmes starting in the autumn term [S2][S5][S8]. You must also participate in any entrance exams you are invited to [S2][S8]. If you do not apply for admission to education, turn down a place of study, or stop your studies, an obligation to work will be imposed on you, meaning you cannot receive unemployment benefits until you meet certain conditions [S6].

results.question: Kela paid me labour market subsidy before May 2026. Will they check my income now?
results.answer:
If Kela paid you basic unemployment allowance or labour market subsidy without a means test before you were transferred to the general social security benefit on 1 May 2026, Kela will check your income by 30 September 2026 to see how much of it affects the means test [S2]. 

After your income is determined, it will affect the next payment period of your general social security benefit [S2]. The means test only applies to future payments and does not retroactively reduce the benefit amount [S2]. Kela will contact you if necessary and will send a separate decision notice if your benefit must be reduced [S2].

Note: The labour market subsidy was abolished when Kela began paying the general social security benefit on 1 May 2026. [S9]

results.question: what is yleistuki
results.answer:
The general social security benefit (yleistuki) is an unemployment benefit paid by Kela [S2][S5]. It is intended for unemployed jobseekers who do not qualify for or have used up their earnings-related unemployment allowance [S2][S5]. 

To get yleistuki, you must meet the following criteria:
- be 18–64 years old [S5]
- be registered as an unemployed jobseeker with employment services [S5]
- live permanently in Finland [S5]
- be available for work on the labour market [S6].

Yleistuki is paid for 5 days a week [S5]. It will replace the labour market subsidy and basic unemployment allowance starting 1 May 2026 [S2].
